title: Phoenician trading posts established
description: Phoenicians founded coastal trading settlements along the North African coast, including sites that would grow into key ports of the region.

title: Kingdom of Numidia unified under Massinissa
description: After the Battle of Zama, Massinissa unified the Berber kingdom of Numidia, a powerful state allied with Rome in present-day Algeria.

title: Arab Muslim conquest of the Maghreb
description: Umayyad forces took the region from the Byzantines, beginning the Islamization and Arabization of North Africa.

title: Ottoman rule begins in Algiers
description: The corsair Barbarossa brought Algiers under Ottoman protection, establishing the Regency of Algiers for three centuries.

title: French conquest of Algiers
description: France invaded and captured Algiers, beginning 132 years of colonial rule and large-scale settlement.

title: Algerian War of Independence begins
description: The FLN launched an armed struggle against French colonial rule on 1 November 1954, sparking a brutal eight-year war.

title: Algeria gains independence from France
description: After a costly war, Algeria became independent on 5 July 1962, ending French colonial rule.

title: Portuguese explorer Diogo Cão reaches the Congo
description: Portuguese navigators arrived at the mouth of the Congo River, opening contact with the Kingdom of Kongo and the Angolan coast.

title: Portuguese found Luanda
description: Paulo Dias de Novais established São Paulo de Loanda, which became the colonial capital and a major slave-trade port.

title: Queen Njinga resists Portuguese expansion
description: Queen Njinga of Ndongo and Matamba led decades of resistance and diplomacy against Portuguese colonization.

title: Angolan War of Independence begins
description: Armed uprisings against Portuguese rule erupted in 1961, beginning a long liberation struggle.

title: Angola gains independence from Portugal
description: Angola became independent on 11 November 1975, though independence was followed by a prolonged civil war.

title: End of the Angolan Civil War
description: The death of UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi led to a ceasefire, ending 27 years of civil war.

title: Rise of the Kingdom of Dahomey
description: The powerful Kingdom of Dahomey emerged on the Abomey plateau, becoming a major regional state.

title: Dahomey conquers Whydah port
description: King Agaja captured the coastal port of Whydah, giving Dahomey control of a key Atlantic slave-trade outlet.

title: France conquers Dahomey
description: After two Franco-Dahomean wars, France defeated King Béhanzin and incorporated Dahomey into its colonial empire.

title: Dahomey gains independence
description: The Republic of Dahomey became independent from France on 1 August 1960.

title: Country renamed Benin
description: Under President Mathieu Kérékou the nation was renamed the People's Republic of Benin.

title: Peaceful democratic transition
description: Benin held multiparty elections after a national conference, becoming an early model of democratic transition in Africa.

title: Founding of the Bangwato state
description: Tswana chiefdoms such as the Bangwato consolidated power, shaping the political landscape of the region.

title: Bechuanaland Protectorate established
description: Britain declared a protectorate over Bechuanaland, partly at the request of Tswana chiefs seeking protection.

title: Three Chiefs travel to Britain
description: Chiefs Khama III, Sebele I, and Bathoen I petitioned London to keep Bechuanaland under Crown rather than company control.

title: Botswana gains independence
description: Botswana became an independent republic on 30 September 1966, with Seretse Khama as its first president.

title: Discovery of diamonds at Orapa
description: Major diamond deposits were found at Orapa, transforming Botswana into one of Africa's fastest-growing economies.

title: Okavango Delta named UNESCO site
description: The Okavango Delta became Botswana's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized as a globally important wetland.

title: Mossi kingdoms flourish
description: The Mossi states such as Ouagadougou and Yatenga dominated the region with organized cavalry-based kingdoms.

title: French conquest of the Mossi
description: France captured Ouagadougou and brought the Mossi kingdoms under colonial control.

title: Colony of Upper Volta created
description: France established the colony of Upper Volta within French West Africa.

title: Upper Volta gains independence
description: Upper Volta became independent from France on 5 August 1960.

title: Renamed Burkina Faso by Thomas Sankara
description: President Thomas Sankara renamed the country Burkina Faso, meaning 'Land of Upright People', and launched social reforms.

title: Popular uprising ousts Compaoré
description: Mass protests forced President Blaise Compaoré to resign after 27 years in power.

title: Kingdom of Burundi consolidates
description: Under Ntare Rushatsi and successors, the Kingdom of Burundi grew into a centralized monarchy ruled by a mwami.

title: Incorporated into German East Africa
description: Burundi was absorbed into German East Africa, with the monarchy retained under indirect rule.

title: Belgian occupation begins
description: Belgian forces occupied Burundi during World War I, later administering it under a League of Nations mandate.

title: Burundi gains independence
description: Burundi became independent on 1 July 1962, initially as a constitutional monarchy.

title: Monarchy abolished, republic declared
description: A coup ended the monarchy and Burundi was proclaimed a republic.

title: First democratic president assassinated
description: The assassination of Melchior Ndadaye, Burundi's first elected Hutu president, triggered a long civil war.

title: Civil war ends with new constitution
description: A power-sharing constitution and elections largely ended Burundi's civil war.

title: Portuguese discover uninhabited islands
description: Portuguese navigators reached the uninhabited Cape Verde archipelago in the mid-15th century.

title: Settlement of Ribeira Grande founded
description: Portuguese settlers founded Ribeira Grande on Santiago, the first permanent European town in the tropics.

title: Hub of the transatlantic slave trade
description: Cape Verde became a key Atlantic entrepôt linking Africa, Europe, and the Americas through the slave trade.

title: PAIGC founded by Amílcar Cabral
description: Amílcar Cabral co-founded the PAIGC to seek independence for Cape Verde and Guinea-Bissau from Portugal.

title: Cape Verde gains independence
description: Cape Verde became independent from Portugal on 5 July 1975.

title: First multiparty elections
description: Cape Verde held its first multiparty elections, becoming one of Africa's most stable democracies.

title: Portuguese reach the Wouri estuary
description: Portuguese explorers named the river Rio dos Camarões ('River of Prawns'), the origin of the country's name.

title: German protectorate of Kamerun established
description: Germany signed treaties with coastal chiefs and established the colony of Kamerun.

title: British and French partition Cameroon
description: After defeating Germany in WWI, Britain and France divided Cameroon into separate mandates.

title: French Cameroon gains independence
description: French Cameroon became independent on 1 January 1960 as the Republic of Cameroon.

title: Reunification with British Southern Cameroons
description: Following a plebiscite, British Southern Cameroons joined to form a federal republic.

title: Indomitable Lions reach World Cup quarterfinals
description: Cameroon's national football team became the first African side to reach a World Cup quarterfinal.

title: Region depopulated by slave raids
description: Sultanates and traders conducted extensive slave raids across the area before colonial rule.

title: France establishes Ubangi-Shari
description: France created the territory of Ubangi-Shari, later part of French Equatorial Africa.

title: Kongo-Wara rebellion against French rule
description: A major rural uprising, the Kongo-Wara or 'War of the Hoe Handle', challenged French colonial exploitation.

title: Central African Republic gains independence
description: The Central African Republic became independent from France on 13 August 1960.

title: Bokassa proclaims an empire
description: President Jean-Bédel Bokassa declared himself emperor, renaming the country the Central African Empire until 1979.

title: Touadéra elected after civil conflict
description: Faustin-Archange Touadéra won elections aimed at restoring stability after years of sectarian conflict.

title: Iron-working Sao civilization emerges
description: The Sao culture flourished near Lake Chad, known for its terracotta and bronze artistry.

title: Rise of the Kanem Empire
description: The Kanem Empire emerged northeast of Lake Chad, becoming a major trans-Saharan trading power.

title: Kanem ruler converts to Islam
description: Mai Humai of Kanem adopted Islam, linking the empire to the wider Muslim world and trade networks.

title: French defeat Rabih az-Zubayr
description: France defeated the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr at Kousséri, paving the way for colonization of Chad.

title: Chad gains independence
description: Chad became independent from France on 11 August 1960.

title: Oil exports begin via Chad-Cameroon pipeline
description: Chad began exporting crude oil through a pipeline to the Atlantic coast, reshaping its economy.

title: Early settlement by Bantu and Arab traders
description: The Comoros islands were settled by Bantu-speaking peoples and integrated into Indian Ocean trade networks.

title: Portuguese reach the Comoros
description: Portuguese explorers arrived in the islands during their expansion into the Indian Ocean.

title: France colonizes Mayotte
description: France acquired the island of Mayotte, beginning its gradual colonization of the Comoros archipelago.

title: Comoros declares independence
description: Three of the four main islands declared independence from France on 6 July 1975.

title: Union of the Comoros constitution adopted
description: A new constitution created the Union of the Comoros with rotating presidency among the islands.

title: Mayotte votes to become French department
description: Mayotte voted to become an overseas department of France, a status the Comoros continues to dispute.

title: Kingdom of Kongo flourishes
description: The powerful Kingdom of Kongo dominated the region around the lower Congo River.

title: Brazza founds Brazzaville
description: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signed treaties with the Téké and founded Brazzaville for France.

title: Capital of French Equatorial Africa
description: Brazzaville became the federal capital of French Equatorial Africa.

title: Republic of the Congo gains independence
description: The Republic of the Congo became independent from France on 15 August 1960.

title: Marxist People's Republic proclaimed
description: Congo became the People's Republic of the Congo, adopting Marxist-Leninist policies for two decades.

title: Civil war returns Sassou Nguesso to power
description: A short civil war ended with Denis Sassou Nguesso reclaiming the presidency.

title: Founding of the Kingdom of Kongo
description: The Kingdom of Kongo arose as a major centralized state spanning parts of the modern DR Congo and Angola.

title: Portuguese reach the Congo River
description: Diogo Cão became the first European to reach the Congo River mouth, opening contact with the Kongo kingdom.

title: Congo Free State under King Leopold II
description: King Leopold II of Belgium claimed the Congo as his private state, leading to notorious colonial atrocities.

title: Belgium takes over the Congo
description: International outcry forced Leopold to transfer the colony to the Belgian state as the Belgian Congo.

title: Congo gains independence
description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo became independent from Belgium on 30 June 1960, with Patrice Lumumba as prime minister.

title: Mobutu seizes power
description: Joseph-Désiré Mobutu took power in a coup, later renaming the country Zaire and ruling for over three decades.

title: Mobutu ousted, country renamed
description: Laurent-Désiré Kabila overthrew Mobutu and renamed the nation the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Spread of Islam along the coast
description: Islam reached the Horn of Africa coast through Arab traders, deeply shaping local society.

title: France acquires Obock
description: France purchased the port of Obock, beginning its colonial presence on the Gulf of Tadjoura.

title: French Somaliland established
description: France consolidated its holdings into French Somaliland, with Djibouti city as its center.

title: Addis Ababa-Djibouti railway completed
description: The railway linking Ethiopia to the port of Djibouti was completed, boosting regional trade.

title: Djibouti gains independence
description: Djibouti became independent from France on 27 June 1977.

title: First foreign military bases established
description: Djibouti's strategic location led to foreign military bases, making it a key hub for global naval operations.
